name: Hans-Ueli Rihs
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Hans-Ueli Rihs is Swiss hearing aid manufacturer Sonova's second largest individual shareholder, with a 6% stake.

With fellow billionaire Beda Diethelm, Rihs and his brother Andy (d. 2018), grew Sonova into the world's largest hearing aid manufacturer, after their father Ernest (d. 1980) bought the company in 1965.
Sonova, which is publicly traded on the SIX Swiss Exchange, generated nearly $4 billion of revenue in fiscal 2024.
Rihs also owns privately-held Swiss Casinos AG, which operates four casinos in Switzerland, and  Swiss soccer team BSC Young Boys.

name: Miranda Qu
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2025); Forbes annual (2022-2025)
forbes_bio: Miranda Qu is the president of Shanghai-based social and e-commerce company Xiaohongshu, which translates as "Little Red Book."
She cofounded the company in 2013 with Charlwin Mao, who is CEO. Xiaohongshu now has over 200 million monthly active users.
Qu and Mao each own an estimated 10% of the company.
Xiaohongshu was valued at $20 billion after a funding round in November 2021 that raised money from investors like Tencent and Alibaba.
Qu formerly worked in marketing for Bertelsmann.

name: Lu Zongjun
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026); Hurun China (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: Lu Zongjun is a director of Shanghai Zhonggu Logistics, a container shipping company in China. He stepped down as chairman in November 2023.
Zhonggu went public at the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2020.
Lu holds a graduate degree from the Wuhan University of Technology.

name: Chen Jinghong
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun China (2017-2026); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Chen Jinghong chairs Huada Automotive Technology, a Shanghai-listed auto parts company based in Jiangsu province.
Chen was the head of a furniture factory, which became the predecessor of Huada, before the company entered into the auto parts business in the 1990s.
His son-in-law Ge Jianghong is CEO of the company.

name: Sven Hagströmer
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2025); Hurun Global (2023-2026)
forbes_bio: Sven Hagstr?mer is the founder and chairman of publicly traded investment company Creades and online broker Avanza.
Hagstr?mer co-founded HQ AB, later HQ Bank, in 1990. The bank collapsed in 2010 because of an overvalued trading portfolio.
Creades was one of the first investors in Klarna, investing as early as 2007, but sold their stake in 2014.
Hagstr?mer was, for the first three seasons, one of the sharks in the Swedish version of Shark Tank.
Hagstr?mer cofounded the Raoul Wallenberg Academy, a non-profit foundation that supports and educates young people in human rights and self-leadership.

name: Lin Por-Chun
sec_insider_companies: ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. (ASX) - GM, ASE Shanghai & Electronics
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Hurun China (2021-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Lin Por-Chun is an executive director of Taiwan Glass, one of Asia's largest glass suppliers.
The company was founded in 1964 by his late father, Lin Yu-Chia, who took it public nine years later.
It has five plants in Taiwan and 15 in mainland China after expanding into the region in 1993.
Por-Chun's brother Por-Fong serves as the company's chairman; another brother Por-Shih is its president and CEO.

name: David Feffer
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026)
forbes_bio: David Feffer is the eldest son of Max Feffer, whose immigrant father Leon Feffer launched the family business.
His grandfather Leon Feffer founded Brazilian pulp and paper firm Suzano in 1924.
David and his three brothers - Daniel, Jorge and Ruben - each inherited shares in Suzano; David and Daniel are also board members of the company.
Suzano acquired Fibria in January 2019 for about $7.5 billion, creating Brazil's largest paper producer.
David is president of Suzano's board of directors and has headed the family's investment arm since 2003.
forbes_facts: Feffer began working for his family's company just before his eighteenth birthday.
He became the chief executive of Suzano in 2001, but later decided to step down and give the position to a non-family member.

name: Ma Hong
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2020); Forbes annual (2015-2021); Hurun Global (2016-2026); Hurun China (2011-2026)
forbes_bio: Ma Hong chairs Raytron Technology, a supplier of infrared imaging and sensor in the eastern Chinese city of Yantai.
Ma Hong holds a doctorate from Huazhong University of Science & Technology.
Raytron Technology listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2019.

name: Alexander Mamut
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Alexander Mamut was trained as a lawyer but made his fortune as an investor.
Over the years he's had stakes in a few banks, an insurance company, fertilzer producer and mobile phone chain.
He was an owner of Rambler&Co, which unites several internet media projects including news site lenta.ru and politics and society site gazeta.ru.
Mamut bought two of Russia's biggest movie chains, Cinema Park and Formula Kino, in 2017.
He eventually sold off his stakes in Russian companies and bought shares in such American companies as Google and Apple.
forbes_facts: In the 1990s, Mamut was close to Russian president Boris Yeltsin and was known as "the Yeltsin family banker."
Mamut owns the British bookstore chain Waterstones, founded by his friend Tim Waterstone, which merged with Barnes & Noble In 2019.
